subject: Re: [stan-users] estimating run time upper limit?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] estimating run time upper limit?
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

On 1/4/14, 6:52 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
>> Ideally, we'd be able to provide an ongoing estimate
>> of the remaining time until completion.
>
> Doable; add it to the list.

Well said :-)

>> The problem I see with the current estimate is that it
>> gives you time for 10 leapfrog steps, but we
>> don't know how many leapfrog steps are going to be needed.
>> At the upper limit, maybe 1000 and at the lower limit, 1.
>> So it doesn't really give you an idea of how long the
>> runs are going to be.
>
> Sure, but again the warning was never intended to be taken
> that precisely. It's original intention was to prevent people
> from spinning of runs that would take weeks without any
> warning.

I understand that, but we need to somehow convey that intent
to the users, who are really looking for a "how long will my
model take to run" estimate. Users have
a tendency to overinterpret everything we output as being
more precise or serious than it is.
This is the same problem we've had all along with
the rejection warnings --- they say one thing and the users
interpret them another way.

- Bob
